ESDC is undertaking a project to convert the round area outside of the 4th floor mailroom into a new kitchen and lunchroom facility. The project will include a full renovation of the existing space, including demolition and installation of new flooring, wall finishes, ceilings, lighting, and all associated architectural finishes. The consultant shall assess existing site conditions and verify that available record drawings accurately reflect current conditions through a comprehensive site investigation. It is anticipated that floor levelling may be required prior to construction. The new lunchroom shall be designed to accommodate a minimum occupancy of 24 persons and will include all required millwork, appliances, and furniture, including countertops with cupboards, space for three microwaves (with at least one microwave located at an accessible height), two full-size refrigerators, tables, and chairs. The client will be procuring all the tables, chairs, fridges and microwaves for this project but the locations of these items must be noted in the design. The project scope shall also include the purchase and installation of centralized waste stations to support waste diversion and recycling initiatives. Acoustic design considerations shall be incorporated to minimize noise transfer to the adjacent mailroom and nearby workstation areas. The project will also include all necessary electrical, mechanical, plumbing, fire protection, and HVAC modifications required to support the new kitchen and lunchroom functions. The consultant shall perform heat load calculations and assess heating, cooling, and ventilation requirements for the renovated space. The design is expected to include a dedicated hot water tank to provide domestic hot water service on the floor; however, the tenant will be responsible for the ongoing operation, maintenance, and replacement of the hot water tank following project completion. The design shall also incorporate low-flow faucets at all sinks to support water conservation objectives. The consultant shall prepare demolition and new construction drawings for all affected disciplines and ensure that the design complies with all applicable codes, standards, and regulatory requirements. The consultant shall apply the latest accessibility standards and best practices to deliver a comprehensive barrier-free design that supports equitable access for all users. As the project involves modifications to the potable water system, potable water sampling and testing shall be completed both before and after construction as part of the project scope. The consultant will be responsible for coordinating all investigations, design development, and documentation necessary to deliver a fully functional, accessible, sustainable, and code-compliant kitchen and lunchroom facility.

Notice is hereby given by the Corporation of the District of North Cowichan (DNC) of its intent to directly award Crofton Lake Dam Geotechnical Investigation Work Plan to Thurber Engineering Limited. The Crofton Lake Dam consists of a main dam and a “saddle” dam originally constructed in the 1950’s based on an engineered design for earth dams. The main dam is about 220 metres long and the saddle dam is about 150 metres long. The dams range from about 1.5 metres to about 5 metres in height. It’s probable that much of the saddle dam predates the 1950’s. Together, the dams allow water retention over a 25-hectare area recognized as Crofton Lake. The dams have failure consequence classifications of “High”. The site is located within a forested area about 1 kilometer away from residences along a rough resource road that is not open to vehicle traffic but is to pedestrians, cyclists and horseback. A dam safety review has recommended a comprehensive site investigation of the materials used in construction to assist with improving predictions of dam breach, seismic stability, settlement and expectations for raising the dams to suit an inundation study and safety review requirements. The work plan requires an Invasive Investigation Plan with an Interim Dam Safety Risk Management Plan, permitting, and includes utility locates, review of historical documents, drilling through the existing dam.

Aperçu de la portée des travaux : Le projet consiste à remplacer sept thermopompes dans les commerces du Complexe Guy-Favreau (Dentiste, Photoflash, Herbes de Chine, Coiffeur, IdentoGO, Biron et Delizia) en priorité. Ces unités fonctionnent au réfrigérant R22 et la plupart sont défectueuses ou non fonctionnelles. Il faudra relocaliser la thermopompe de la dentisterie puisqu'elle est localisée au-dessus d'une chaise d'examen, donc pas accessible facilement pour effectuer son entretien. Une mise aux normes des thermopompes pourrait être requise pour leur installation (alimentation en eau, raccordement au drain, conformité parasismique, etc.). La thermopompe du commerce Herbe de Chine est fort possiblement surdimensionnée et sa capacité devra être réévaluée, de même que le raccordement au drain qui ne semble pas conforme. Le remplacement de ces thermopompes pourra aussi faire l’objet d’une demande de subvention, à effectuer par l’expert-conseil. De nouvelles thermopompes fonctionnant au R32 sont à privilégier. Il faut considérer les modèles de la marque ClimateMaster fonctionnant au R454b, soit un modèle de thermopompe de format et configuration à peu près similaire aux thermopompes existantes. Également, les modèles de la marque Daikin fonctionnant au R32, soit un modèle nouvellement installé et dont certaines thermopompes sont disponibles en inventaire pour une installation plus rapide, peuvent aussi constituer un choix intéressant mais celles-ci sont plus volumineuses. Les entrées d'eau et les sorties de drainage ne se situent pas du même côté sur le modèle de thermopompe Daikin, ou encore un kit d'inversion dans le boîtier pourrait possiblement être demandé aux plans et devis et sur les dessins d'atelier pour faciliter leur branchement et ainsi possiblement éviter l’ajout de pompes de condensat. Un hygiéniste industriel sera mandaté par BGIS pour échantillonner les matériaux touchés par les travaux. Cet expert-conseil tiers sera déterminé à la suite du présent appel d’offres. Aucun honoraire en lien avec l’hygiène industriel ne doit être inclus dans la soumission pour le présent appel d’offres. Aussi, une mise à jour du PGLL (programme de gestion de lutte contre la Legionella) sera aussi requise, mais celle-ci sera effectuée par BGIS. Aucun honoraire en lien le PGLL ne doit être inclus dans la soumission pour le présent appel d’offres. L’expert-conseil devra avant tout effectuer un relevé dans les commerces, à prévoir en soirée, afin de valider les conditions existantes. L’expert-conseil devra ensuite rédiger un programme technique de conception (se référer à l’annexe D.6 pour plus de détails sur ce document) et formuler une recommandation des travaux recommandés (remplacement des thermopompes existante et mise aux normes de leur installation), accompagné d’une estimation de classe D. La préparation des plans et devis (versions 66%, 99% et émission pour soumission) sera requise, en fournissant une estimation de classe A. L’Expert-conseil devra ensuite compléter les phases d’appel d’offres Entrepreneurs et de construction.

The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requires services for the preventive maintenance and repair of medical equipment at all CSC institutions in the Quebec region. This service is necessary to comply with Accreditation Canada's Required Safety Practices as well as manufacturers' recommendations, to ensure that the equipment is functional and effective throughout its lifespan. They also contribute to providing safe and secure health services to clients. Objectives: The Contractor must provide preventive maintenance and repair services for medical equipment by supplying the qualified labour, expertise, products, accessories, tools, equipment, and transportation to carry out the work. Submit the list for review before each visit. Keep an updated list of tools and equipment throughout the work. c) Provide one invoice per institution, once the project manager has approved the submitted reports.
